intestinal transplant rejection is associated with innate and adaptive immune responses to enteric bacteria and donor alloantigens, whereas stable grafts are associated with a lack of these responses.

intestinal transplantation recipients are not immune tolerant to the graft, as has been suggested in the literature, but rather are unresponsive to donor antigens, which may have important implications for the design of future immunosuppressive protocols.
